jobs.title: Technical Project Manager
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE
GridUnity is the industry leader in interconnection life cycle management, delivering cutting-edge software solutions that eliminate bottlenecks in the interconnection process and accelerate the transition to a more affordable, sustainable, and resilient energy future.
Our Mission
We unite all grid interconnection stakeholders on a single platform that converts centralized data into actionable intelligence and accelerates the transition to a reliable, sustainable, and cost-efficient electric grid.
GridUnity is a trusted partner to leading utilities, grid operators, and policymakers. Our technology solutions tackle the interconnection queue backlog by significantly reducing processing times. Whether cutting transmission interconnection timelines from years to months or enabling distribution applications to be processed within a day, we help accelerate energy projects at every scale.
Our Vision
Energizing the planet with a faster, smarter, and more sustainable grid.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
As Technical Project Manager, you will plan and drive complex, cross-team delivery across GridUnity’s engineering organization. You will help shape scope, timing, and phasing with Customer Success, Product and Engineering, then own the path from that plan to a successful release: turning goals into plans, surfacing dependencies and risks early, and keeping work moving across teams.
This is a technical role. You will understand the architecture, integrations, and environments behind the work well enough to ask the right questions, challenge estimates, and help engineers resolve blockers. You will partner with engineering leadership on planning, capacity, and delivery practices, and with Product, Engineering, Quality Engineering, and Customer Experience on scope, timing, and customer commitments.
Your success will be reflected in predictable delivery, fewer late surprises, and stakeholders who trust the status they receive because it is clear, current, and grounded in evidence.
PLAN AND DRIVE DELIVERY
 - Lead planning for cross-team initiatives and releases, turning goals and scope into milestones, sequencing, and clear ownership.
 - Work with engineering leads to break down work, validate estimates, and build plans that reflect real capacity, dependencies, and risk.
 - Run engineering team ceremonies and the broader delivery cadence for your programs, including sprint planning, daily standups, backlog refinement, sprint reviews, retrospectives, dependency reviews, and release readiness reviews. Keep meetings purposeful and decisions recorded.
 - Establish a clear definition of ready and definition of done with Product and Engineering. Ensure work meets the definition of ready before a sprint commits to it, and meets the definition of done before it is considered complete.
 - Track progress against plan in Jira and related tools, keeping boards, epics, and roadmaps accurate enough to support real decisions.
 - Identify blockers early and drive them to resolution, escalating through the established path when a decision is needed.
MANAGE TECHNICAL RISK AND DEPENDENCIES
 - Understand the architecture, integrations, data flows, and environments behind each initiative well enough to anticipate where work will get hard.
 - Map dependencies across teams, systems, and third parties, and make sure each one has an owner and a date.
 - Maintain a living risk log for your programs, with likelihood, impact, mitigation, and accountable owners.
 - Partner with Quality Engineering to align validation plans and exit criteria with the release plan before deadlines are committed.
 - Coordinate release and deployment planning with Engineering and DevOps, including cutover steps, rollback plans, and customer-facing timing.
COMMUNICATE AND ALIGN STAKEHOLDERS
 - Provide clear, regular status to engineering leadership, Product, and Customer Experience: what is on track, what is at risk, and what decision is needed.
 - Make tradeoffs between scope, timing, and quality visible, and help stakeholders make informed decisions rather than discovering them late.
 - Translate technical detail into language that nontechnical stakeholders and customer-facing teams can act on.
 - Support customer implementation and utility-facing commitments by keeping delivery dates realistic and changes communicated early.
IMPROVE HOW WE DELIVER
 - Partner with engineering leadership to improve planning, estimation, capacity management, and delivery practices across teams.
 - Define and use meaningful delivery measures, such as predictability against plan, cycle time, dependency lead time, and release outcomes.
 - Lead retrospectives on major initiatives and follow through on improvements that reduce recurring delays.
 - Use AI-assisted tools where they improve planning, reporting, or coordination, with appropriate review so their output is trusted only when it has been checked.
 - Share effective practices across GridUnity’s product lines, adapting the approach to each team’s size, maturity, and risk profile.
WHAT YOU’LL BRING
REQUIRED KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES
 - 6+ years of experience in technical project management, program management, software engineering, or a related technical delivery role, including 3+ years managing cross-team software initiatives.
 - A track record of delivering complex SaaS releases on time by building realistic plans, managing dependencies, and adapting as conditions change.
 - Enough technical depth to understand system architecture, APIs, integrations, environments, and CI/CD workflows, and to engage credibly with engineers on design and estimation.
 - Experience running Agile delivery (Scrum, Kanban, or a hybrid) and adapting processes to fit the team rather than the other way around.
 - Proficiency with Jira or comparable tools for planning, tracking, and reporting on work across multiple teams.
 - Ability to identify, quantify, and communicate risk, and to drive decisions on scope, timing, and quality tradeoffs.
 - Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to give concise status to executives and detailed direction to engineering teams.
 - Comfort leading through influence: aligning people who do not report to you around shared plans and priorities.
 - Strong organizational skills and follow-through, with a habit of making ownership and next steps explicit.

 - Scale & Governance: Track record of maturing delivery processes or establishing project management frameworks within expanding SaaS organizations.

jobs.description:
GiveWell’s mission is to help people in need as much as we can by researching the most cost‑effective ways to save and improve lives, sharing our work openly, and directing donations to the programs we believe will do the most good. Our work, which focuses on global health and well-being, is funded by tens of thousands of donors who rely on our research to inform their giving. We’ve grown from directing $1.5 million in 2010 to directing more than $400 million in 2025. We anticipate our total grantmaking is likely to approach or even exceed $1 billion this year, and we are working toward a future that could be several times that scale. Through years of deliberate groundwork, we’ve been growing our research capacity and scope in order to direct substantially more funding to the most impactful opportunities we can find. 
 Manager, IT & Technology Operations
 GiveWell is a research organization that identifies and funds cost-effective giving opportunities, focusing on global health and well-being. Our work is funded by tens of thousands of donors who rely on our research to inform their giving. We’ve grown from directing $1.5 million in 2010 to directing more than $400 million in 2025.
 GiveWell’s ~130 (and growing!) staff are researchers, grantmakers, and fundraisers who are technically fluent, move quickly, and adopt new tools earlier than most organizations our size. When our technology fails or slows us down, the cost isn’t just frustration, but time sacrificed finding and funding interventions that save and improve lives. We’re hiring a Manager of IT and Technology Operations who will design a support program well above the typical corporate IT experience, make informed decisions about where to invest our time and resources, and bring the entire organization along. Standard IT management isn’t enough here. We need someone who understands why GiveWell is different and builds IT that supports it.
 Why is GiveWell hiring for this position now? 
 Our technology team has grown from a small group of generalists into specialized teams. Support, devices, and service quality now need a dedicated leader. On top of that, we are at a decision point on key tools, including our MDM platform and ticketing system. We have staff in Europe without a dedicated coverage plan and no internal after-hours response program. This is a real opportunity to define what excellent IT looks like at an organization where technology delays have a direct cost to impact.
 The Role
 As Manager of IT and Technology Operations, you’ll be the person responsible for making technology work for an impact-focused team. Your team owns the devices, applications, and related tooling that work happens on. One day you are scoping a new MDM platform and the next you’re negotiating a vendor renewal or coaching a specialist through a complex escalation. You’ll lead an existing team while hiring more members, own our device and support infrastructure, and step into support work yourself when it is needed.
 Here are some of the things you’d tackle in this role:
 Lead and develop your team. You’ll manage a team ranging from early-career to senior individual contributors, setting clear expectations, coaching to a high standard, and managing performance directly. Your team is your primary lever, so their growth is one of your most important outcomes.
 Design support for how GiveWell works.  Our staff expect speed and the newest tools, and they lose real impact when they’re blocked. You’ll assess how support is delivered today, recommend the right mix of in-house and vendor support, and lead that transition.
 Make calibrated calls. You’ll decide which problems deserve your team’s energy now, which can wait, and which aren’t worth fighting for. You’ll know where to hold the line (security and donor privacy) and where flexibility is the right path.
 Build a service delivery discipline. Today, we have loose SLAs and no way to measure satisfaction. You’ll define meaningful targets, build a way to measure how support feels to the people receiving it, and manage your team against both. A typical corporate IT playbook won’t work here - we consider the support of our internal teams paramount.
 Own device and endpoint operations. Your team owns the full lifecycle for our Mac-majority fleet. You’ll set our go-forward plan for MDM, whether that means a new build, a migration, or updating what we have.
 Design coverage for a distributed team. We have offices in Oakland, Brooklyn, and London, plus remote staff distributed across North America and Europe (with more expansion to come). You’ll build coverage that works across those geographies and an after-hours incident response capability with a rotation structure and escalation paths.
 Own procurement. You’ll own the budget and forecast for hardware and core software, hold signing and renewal authority for those vendors, and negotiate contracts. You’ll make, and be accountable for, spending decisions.
 Protect our data and our donors’ trust . GiveWell has spent years building trust with donors, grantees, and employees, which is critical to sustain. You will implement and maintain access controls, device security, and data handling practices across the systems you own.
 What’s not part of this role today: Salesforce, our website, data analytics, and AI enablement sit with other teams. These will be partners of yours, but not within your scope of ownership.
 About You
 The strongest candidates will have 7+ years in IT operations, technology support, or service delivery, including 3+ years managing people. Beyond that, here’s what we’re really looking for:
 You connect IT decisions to impact. You think GiveWell is doing something special, not just “doing good”, and that matters to you personally. You can explain how a slow laptop refresh or a clunky access request turns into lost research and fundraising time, and you ensure that shapes your priorities. 
 You manage people directly and well. When it comes to feedback, you operate on the principle that clear is kind. You’ve helped people grow to a higher standard than they were held to before. You’ve also made the call when someone wasn’t the right fit. You’ll join a team that already exists and you are ready to build a strong relationship with your new staff and hire top talent. 
 You have calibrated judgment. You know what to focus on and what to let go. You can name a time you chose not to enforce a standard because the cost to users outweighed the benefit, and a time you held firm. 
 You've designed IT for tech-savvy users. You’ve built (or reshaped) a support function for people who expect a lot, not just kept the lights on and maintained the status quo. You think about support as a system to be designed, set standards for, measured against, and adapted to what your users need.

jobs.description:
Our Purpose 
 At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.
 About Us 
 SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.
 Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.
 What Are We Looking For? 
 We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.
 As a Project Manager, Services Technology & Tooling, you will be tasked with helping make our expanded global partnership successful for customers by coordinating the operational technology required for the SentinelOne and partner services relationship. This partnership brings together SentinelOne's AI-powered security platform and our partners' expertise in managed detection and response, managed SIEM, and incident response, and as partner-delivered services grow, SentinelOne remains committed to clear customer ownership, technical quality, and measurable results. This is a delivery-focused program role managing the workstreams covering approved platform access, tenant and environment architecture, integrations, workflow tooling, and technical cutover readiness, requiring disciplined coordination across IT, InfoSec, Product, service operations, and partner technical teams without bypassing security or access controls to meet schedule dates.
 What Will You Do?
 Primary responsibilities include:
 Develop and maintain an integrated technology and tooling workplan with milestones, dependencies, owners, and decisions.
 Coordinate SentinelOne and partner stakeholders on approved platform access, tenant models, environment configuration, and integration needs.
 Track systems and operational tooling readiness for intake, provisioning, reporting, case handling, and service workflows.
 Ensure access requests, security approvals, ownership changes, and data-handling controls are documented and completed through authorized channels.
 Drive integration tests, cutover checklists, go/no-go reviews, and post-transition issue tracking.
 Surface schedule risks, blocked dependencies, and competing technical priorities to workstream leaders early.
 Maintain project status, action logs, risk registers, decision records, and executive-ready reporting.
 Work with Support, Professional Services, IT, Product, Security, and partner teams to resolve cross-system issues.
 Capture the final access model, integration documentation, and operational handoff required for steady-state support.
 Deliver against the role's success measures: timely completion of technology cutover and integration milestones; approved access provisioned accurately and on schedule; no avoidable security-control gaps introduced by the transition; clear readiness evidence and accountable closure of tooling defects; and a stable handoff from project execution to steady-state system ownership.
 What Skills and Knowledge Will You Bring?
 Ideal candidates will have:
 3 or more years of experience in technical project management, business systems implementation, IT delivery, or enterprise platform operations.
 Experience coordinating integrations, access management, technology migrations, or operational tooling launches.
 Familiarity with SaaS platforms, APIs, identity/access concepts, and system dependencies.
 Strong project planning, risk management, stakeholder communication, and structured issue resolution.
 Ability to work effectively with InfoSec and IT controls around customer data and privileged access.
 Proficiency with project tracking, documentation, and collaboration tools.
 Comfort managing parallel workstreams without direct authority and with shifting delivery requirements.
 Experience with Salesforce, customer support systems, service management tooling, or partner access portals is highly desirable.
 Familiarity with security operations tooling and enterprise tenant architectures is highly desirable.
 PMP, Agile, or similar project-management training is highly desirable.
 Why SentinelOne?
 AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment. From day one, we architected an AI-native platform designed to operate at machine speed, not as an add-on to legacy systems but as the foundation itself. If you want to build where innovation and impact move together, this is that place.

This role manages a group of Enablement Specialists, setting their priorities, developing their skills, and holding the team accountable for the operating cadence, AI-enabled workflows, and project execution that drive value-based care performance.
The Manager supports all Lines of Business (LOB) the team engages in, including Medicare Advantage, MSSP, Medicaid, and Commercial value-based care contracts. The Manager balances people leadership with hands-on operational ownership, resolving practice needs as they arise, removing blockers for the team, and translating executive priorities into repeatable systems that scale.
Who We Are:
Aledade PBC, a public benefit corporation, exists to empower the most transformational part of our health care landscape - independent primary care. We were founded in 2014, and since then, we've become the largest network of independent primary care in the country - helping practices, health centers and clinics deliver better care to their patients and thrive in value-based care. Additionally, by creating value-based contracts across a wide variety of health plans, we aim to flip the script on the traditional fee-for-service model. Our work strengthens continuity of care, aligns incentives and ensures primary care physicians are paid for what they do best - keeping patients healthy. If you want to help create a health care system that is good for patients, good for practices and good for society - and if you're eager to join a collaborative, inclusive and remote-first culture - you've come to the right place.

At Aledade PBC, you will be part of a creative culture that is driven by a passion for tackling complex issues with respect, open-mindedness and a desire to learn. COMPANY OVERVIEW
Deepgram is bringing the world’s most natural interface, voice, to the technology we use every day. Our speech models and real-time infrastructure power AI systems that keep up with the way people actually speak. More than 5,000 organizations run conversational voice AI on Deepgram in production, including Twilio, Cloudflare, Sierra, Decagon, Vapi, Cresta, Granola, and Jack in the Box.
The Deepgram Voice Agent Platform brings together speech-to-text, text-to-speech and speech-to-speech, with voice-native foundation models available through cloud APIs or self-hosted and on-premises deployments. Built for accuracy, low latency and cost efficiency, Deepgram makes high-quality voice experiences practical to build and run at scale. More than 650,000 developers have used Deepgram to process more than 200,000 years of audio. Every day, more of the world’s conversations with AI run on our models.
OPERATING PRINCIPLES
Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together:
 1. Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.
 2. Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.
 3. Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.
 4. Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet.
We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.
AI-FIRST BY DEFAULT
We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate.
That means more than using the tools. We expect you to:
 - Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster.
 - Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you.
 - Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.
 - Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place.

What matters is what you can build, and that you want to build it for People.

 - Handle sensitive employee information and unreleased work with sound professional discretion.
Experience

You will use customer sentiment, adoption data, system stability, and infrastructure health to determine whether the program is operating as designed and intervene when it is not. The Implementation Manager remains accountable until the customer meets defined stabilization criteria and is ready for a structured handoff to Customer Success.
 Success in this role means delivering more than an on-time implementation. It means launching a healthy, adopted, sustainable program that customers trust and that creates the foundation for long-term value and expansion.
